newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia said lagging in financial chase.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia said lagging in financial chase.

text.p: Australia faces a very significant gap which it needs to close on its two main competitors in Asia if it is to take a leadership role as an Asia Pacific financial centre, Tom Dunton, managing director of Standard Chartered Asia, told a commodities conference on Monday.
"We are running third (after Hong Kong and Singapore) and not a very close third. We need to pick up the pace," Dunton told the Asia-Pacific Commodities Markets Conference.
He was commenting on the Australian government's ambition of becoming the leading financial centre of Asia, outside Tokyo, by the year 2000.
Australia should develop an agenda for action to deal with issues such as loss of market share, lack of competitiveness and a tax reform, Dunton said.
"Perhaps of greatest importance (is) the attitude or mind set issue (on Aisa) which at present seems rather indifferent," he said.
As rated by both providers and users of financial services, Australia stands significantly behind Hong Kong and Singapore in most relevant categories, he said.

He said studies showed that if Australia could achieve a leading competitive position in financial services, it would increase its terms of trade by a factor of about 1.6 percent and bring about a small general fall in the cost of capital.
The economy would shift to being more capital intensive, GDP would be higher and so would real wages, Dunton said.
Overall economic welfare in terms of present value would increase by about A$25 billion, he said.
